req.title: Register requires username
req.statement: The system shall render the register form with an error message when POST /auth/register omits the username.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /auth/register must render the register form with 'Username is required.' when username is omitted. We need: (1) a positive case confirming a valid registration succeeds (HTTP 302 redirect to /auth/login), (2) a negative case confirming that omitting username yields HTTP 200 with the exact error message 'Username is required.', (3) a boundary case confirming that an empty-string username (the boundary between absent and present) also triggers the error, and (4) additional cases to kill mutations on the boolean condition `if not username`, the exact error string constant, and the redirect target. We also test that a non-empty username does NOT produce the error, catching boolean-negation mutations.

tests.name: test_register_missing_username_returns_error_message
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
actions: POST /auth/register with password='stone' but no username field
expected: HTTP 200 response (form re-rendered, not redirected)
Response body contains exactly 'Username is required.'
trace: R-FLASKR-004: error pathway 'form error: Username is required.'
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'password': 'stone'})
assert r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200, got {r.status_code}'
assert b'Username is required.' in r.data, 'Error message not found in response'

def test_register_missing_username_returns_error_message():
    fd2, path2 = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd2)
    app2 = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path2})
    with app2.app_context():
        init_db()
    c = app2.test_client()
    resp = c.post('/auth/register', data={'password': 'stone'})
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert b'Username is required.' in resp.data

tests.name: test_register_state_transition_missing_username_no_db_insert
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database initialised with init_db() — 5 pre-loaded users exist
actions: Attempt to login with username='' to confirm no user was created
expected: First POST returns HTTP 200 with 'Username is required.'
Subsequent GET /auth/register returns HTTP 200 (system stays in unauthenticated state)
No new user row was inserted (system state unchanged)
trace: R-FLASKR-004: STC — failed registration must not transition system to registered state
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db

def test_register_state_transition_missing_username_no_db_insert():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        user_count_before = get_db().execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user').fetchone()[0]
    client = app.test_client()
    resp = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': '', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert b'Username is required.' in resp.data
    with app.app_context():
        user_count_after = get_db().execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user').fetchone()[0]
    assert user_count_after == user_count_before
    assert user_count_after == 5
